title: Three Mondays and One Short Pointer
subtitle: 学校教育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：lecture　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 lecture 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the professor ① attended the lecture that no student in the hall would have recorded, and he said the attending was the whole of the Monday. The ② lecture, meaning the talk itself and not the pointer, ran three Mondays and stayed unrecorded in the book; a lecture, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ lecture in that hall had the same short pointer beside it, and the ④ lecture at the far platform, meaning the note they kept for the children to take and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A lecture, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the professor said the recording is the part that fills three Mondays.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the lecture was the whole of the matter, meaning the patience and not the talk. The ⑥ lecture, meaning the patience and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; lecture, he said, is either something you attend or the only word that means both a talk and a patience. He said the patience is the part they remember.

By 1983 the ⑦ lecture had become a line in a timetable, and the timetable had become an argument about the short pointer. The ⑧ lecture of the whole thing, the professor wrote in March, was one hall and three Mondays of recording; lecture, he said, is either the note at the far platform or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ lecture I remember is the talk recorded in the timetable, which closed in 1985 and is still recorded as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ lecture, my mother said in 1987, is the only talk that improves by being recorded; every lecture, she said, is a patience that has agreed to look like a talk. She said the patience was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 讲座；讲课（指讲堂里每一场旁边的那一场）
B. n. 讲座；讲课（指那场讲座本身，与教鞭相对）
C. 固定搭配：attend the lecture 听这场讲座
D. n. 讲座；讲课（指留给孩子们记下的那页笔记那一场）
E. n. 讲学之事（抽象总称，指一处讲堂的讲座之事）
F. n. 讲座；讲课（指课程表里写到、被记载的的那一场）
G. n. 耐心、教诲（指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 教诲（抽象总称，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: attended the lecture that no student in the hall would have recorded
The lecture, meaning the talk itself and not the pointer
the lecture at the far platform
the lecture was the whole of the matter
the lecture had become a line in a timetable
The lecture of the whole thing
A lecture, my mother said in 1987

answers.why: attend the lecture 意为“听这场讲座”，1978 年那位教授把讲堂里没有一位学生肯记载的一场讲座做了一遍。
lecture 意为“讲座；讲课”，指那场讲座本身而不是教鞭，它经过了三个星期一而在簿子上没有被记载。
lecture 意为“讲座；讲课”，指讲堂里每一场旁边的那一场，每一场旁边都有同一根细细的教鞭。
lecture 意为“讲座；讲课”，指最远那方讲台留给孩子们记下的那页笔记那一场，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
lecture 意为“耐心、教诲”，指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份教诲就是那件事的全部。
lecture 意为“教诲”，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西而不是那场讲座，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
lecture 意为“讲座；讲课”，指课程表里写到、被记载的的那一场，到 1983 年这一场成了课程表里的一行。
lecture 意为“讲学之事”，教授三月写道，整件事的讲座之事是一处讲堂和三个星期一的记载。
lecture 意为“讲座；讲课”，我记得的是课程表里记载过的那一场，1985 年讲完了，至今仍被说成讲堂里最安静的一场。
lecture 为抽象总称，母亲 1987 年说，讲座是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的讲座。
